target.title: test(qa): redact script evidence diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared script evidence writer bounds logs and failure details, but secret-bearing diagnostics or producer-known private values can be persisted unless redaction occurs before output is discarded. Stream chunk boundaries and oversized raw logs can otherwise remove the context required to recognize a credential while retaining its sensitive tail.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follow-up reuses the public logging redaction contract and adds producer-supplied sensitive values to `createQaScriptEvidenceWriter`. It:

- removes exact sensitive values across child-process chunk boundaries;
- reconstructs bounded raw output before applying built-in and configured logging patterns;
- safely omits oversized unredacted logs instead of truncating away redaction context;
- keeps normalized pass/fail/blocked status controlled by the script result rather than native artifact payloads.

The focused contract tests cover credentials, access tokens, Matrix session keys, recovery material, private message content, default and configured patterns split across chunks, oversized raw logs, and conflicting native artifact status content.

## User Impact

There is no product behavior change. QA maintainers get bounded script evidence that does not persist known secret or private diagnostic content, while normalized status semantics remain unchanged.

## Dependencies

- Builds on the shared script evidence writer merged by #99374.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/script-evidence.test.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/media/hosted-media-provider-live.test.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/plugins/clawhub-release-candidate-install.test.ts` — 33 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwmtgzpm4rhh4vj8enpmgjhv` — changed lint and guard checks passed.
- `oxfmt --check` passed for the two changed files.
- Final Codex autoreview on commit `0931fff0118283ec35213e8b7a9ac39c0c2a0078` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
